title: France wins the UEFA European Championship by defeating Italy, 2–1 following a golden goal in the final game at the Stadion Feijenoord in Rotterdam, Netherlands.
text: Stadion Feijenoord, more commonly known by its nickname De Kuip (pronounced , the Tub), is a stadium in Rotterdam, Netherlands. It was completed in 1937.

title: President: Carlo Azeglio Ciampi
text: Carlo Azeglio Ciampi was an Italian politician, statesman and banker who was the president of Italy from 1999 to 2006 and prime minister of Italy from 1993 to 1994. A World War II veteran, Ciampi had fought for the Italian resistance movement after he evaded capture from the Wehrmacht in 1943.

title: Prime Minister: Massimo D'Alema (until 25 April), Giuliano Amato (starting 25 April)
text: Massimo D'Alema is an Italian politician and journalist who was the 53rd prime minister of Italy from 1998 to 2000. He was Deputy Prime Minister of Italy and Italian Minister of Foreign Affairs from 2006 to 2008.

title: Nagorno-Karabakh Republic
text: Nagorno-Karabakh is a region of West Asia located in the southern part of the Lesser Caucasus range, at the eastern edge of the Armenian Highlands, encompassing the highland part of the wider geographical region known as Karabakh. Under Russian and Soviet rule, the region came to be known as Nagorno-Karabakh, meaning "Mountainous Karabakh" in Russian.

title: “La fine del millennio” by Vasco Rossi
text: Vasco Rossi, also known mononymously as Vasco or with the nickname Il Blasco, is an Italian singer-songwriter and poet. He has published 30 albums (not including unofficial releases) and written over 250 songs, as well as lyrics for other artists.

title: “Move Your Body” by Eiffel 65
text: "Move Your Body" is a song by Italian musical group Eiffel 65. It was released as the third single from their debut album, Europop, on 4 November 1999.

title: “Where I'm Headed” by 27 January
text: "Where I'm Headed" is the eight track on Norwegian singer-songwriter Lene Marlin's debut studio album, Playing My Game. Written by Marlin and produced by Hans G and Jørn Dahl, the song was released as the album's third single in late 1999 following Marlin's international breakthrough hit, "Sitting Down Here".

title: “Cartoon Heroes” by Aqua
text: "Cartoon Heroes" is a song by Danish-Norwegian dance-pop group Aqua from their second studio album, Aquarius. The song was sent to radio stations worldwide on 1 January 2000 and was released as a retail single on 31 January 2000.

title: “Go Let It Out” by Oasis
text: "Go Let It Out" is a song by English rock band Oasis, written by the band's lead guitarist, and chief songwriter, Noel Gallagher. It was released on 7 February 2000 as the first single from their fourth studio album, Standing on the Shoulder of Giants, as well as their first following the departure of rhythm guitarist Bonehead and bassist Guigsy.

title: “Pure Shores” by All Saints
text: "Pure Shores" is a song by English girl group All Saints from their second studio album, Saints & Sinners. Group member Shaznay Lewis and producer William Orbit wrote the song for a scene in the 2000 adventure drama film The Beach.

title: “American Pie” by Madonna
text: "American Pie" is a song by the American singer and songwriter Don McLean. It was a commercial success and cultural touchstone, notable for its extensive and ambiguous lyrics about America's changing society in the 1950s and 1960s.

title: “The Bad Touch” by Bloodhound Gang
text: "The Bad Touch" is a song by American alternative rock band Bloodhound Gang. It was released in September 1999 as the second single from their third studio album, Hooray for Boobies, which was released the following year in the United States and United Kingdom.

title: “Oops!... I Did It Again” by 5 May
text: "Oops!... I Did It Again" is a pop song recorded by American singer Britney Spears from her second studio album of the same name.
listen: Oops!... I Did It Again 5 May

title: “It's My Life” by 12 May
text: "It's My Life" is a song by American rock band Bon Jovi. It was released on May 8, 2000, as the lead single from their seventh studio album, Crush.

title: “Vamos a bailar (Esta vida nueva)” by Paola & Chiara
text: "Vamos a bailar" (transl. "We're Gonna Dance (This New Life)"), also known just as "Vamos a bailar", is a 2000 song composed and performed by Italian duo Paola & Chiara. It is the leading single of the album Television.
listen: Vamos a bailar (Esta vida nueva) Paola & Chiara

title: “Freestyler” by 21 July
text: "Freestyler" is a song by Finnish hip hop group Bomfunk MC's. It was released in Finland on 30 October 1999 as the third single from their debut studio album, In Stereo, and was released internationally in February 2000.

title: “Music” by 18 August
text: "Music" is a song recorded by American singer Madonna for her eighth studio album of the same title. Inspired by a Sting concert Madonna attended, she wrote and produced the song with Mirwais Ahmadzaï.

title: “Fuoco nel fuoco” by Eros Ramazzotti
text: Eros Walter Luciano Ramazzotti is an Italian pop and rock singer, songwriter and record producer. He is popular in Italy and most European countries, and throughout the Spanish-speaking world, as he has released most of his albums in both Italian and Spanish.

title: “Beautiful Day” by 6 October
text: "Beautiful Day" is a song by Irish rock band U2. It is the first track on their tenth studio album, All That You Can't Leave Behind, and was released as the album's lead single on 9 October 2000.

title: “She Bangs” by Ricky Martin
text: "She Bangs" is a song recorded by Puerto Rican singer Ricky Martin for his sixth studio album, Sound Loaded. The song was written by Desmond Child, Walter Afanasieff, and Draco Rosa, while the production was handled by Afanasieff and Rosa.

title: “Shape of My Heart” by Backstreet Boys
text: "Shape of My Heart" is a song by American boy band Backstreet Boys. It was released on October 2, 2000, as the lead single from their fourth studio album, Black & Blue.

text: "Again" is a song by American rock musician Lenny Kravitz, being the only new song from his first Greatest Hits album, released in 2000. title: “Don't Tell Me” by 8 December
text: "Don't Tell Me" is a song recorded by American singer Madonna for her eighth studio album Music. Madonna co-wrote and co-produced the track with Mirwais Ahmadzaï, with additional writing from her brother-in-law, Joe Henry.
